$comment: W11: the slots that draw a product screen, one entry per slot kind. drawn: the width the slot draws its picture at a 1,440- and a 390-px window (CSS px; null where the slot is not drawn), in a light and a dark build (the dark frame's card-indigo mat, night.css, takes 20 px), measured on a build (start: 50b33ed, night E's probe; result: this wave's build). crop: the app view a crop holds (CSS px of the product's 1,440 x 900 window), never wider than the slot draws it in either theme, 2 px to spare (DECISIONS.md D-LEGIBLE; the two sets share their clips, so an auto build marks both alike), 16:10 like the window (the loop's 2:1 band like its frame); phone: the crop a window below the breakpoint loads (D-PHONE-SCREENS), null where the desktop crop serves both widths or the slot is not drawn on a phone. full: the slot draws the whole window on a desktop. serve: the served WebP's width in pixels, twice the widest drawn width plus 2 px for sub-pixel layout, so a device-scale-2 screen gets two pixels per CSS px. quality: the served WebP's quality (default 80; What's new 70: its three images load before the English home's hero paints, and Lighthouse counts their bytes against the LCP budget). focus: per key and picture, the one thing the slot's caption or text names (selector: the first visible match, largest: the largest one; text: the first element whose text matches; card: its nearest bordered box at least this wide; union: several of these together; note: what the crop shows); scripts/capture-screenshots.mjs cuts a clip of the crop's size around it, pad px (default 16) outside it, inside the window: centred when the thing is smaller than the clip (fit start: from its start edge anyway), from its start edge when larger — its left in English, its right in Hebrew (edge end: the other one). Read by the capture script, src/lib/screens.ts and tests/legibility.spec.ts.
